display.purpose: Hero H1 only, one per page.

title.purpose: Card/subsection H3-H4, set in the body face.

body-sm.purpose: Card body text and secondary prose (0.9375rem).

caption.purpose: Footer links, stat labels, secondary captions (0.8125rem).

micro.purpose: Trust lines and status badges (0.6875rem mono); never running text.

label.purpose: Mono uppercase precision marker: eyebrows, stats, meta captions, dates.

shadows.name: header-scroll
shadows.purpose: Sticky header separation once the page has scrolled; fully transparent at rest.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default easing for all transitions/reveals; exponential ease-out, no bounce.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Hover/focus micro-transitions (borders, color, arrow nudge, hover enter).

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Reveal-on-scroll, card lift settle (hover exit), list staggers.

motion.name: dur-entrance
motion.purpose: Page/card entrances: hero copy stagger and ledger-card rise. Signature accent-draw (scaleX from left, 500-600ms) is the one drawn-line moment per page.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Sole large-surface use of the orange gradient; the main CTA everywhere on the site.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; background: linear-gradient(90deg, #FF4A38 0%, #FF7B4D 100%); color: #fff; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1rem; text-decoration: none; border: none; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; transition: filter 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #C2410C; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Outline button for secondary actions alongside a primary CTA.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; background: transparent; color: #22282C; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 1rem; text-decoration: none; border: 1px solid #E7E3DC; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; transition: border-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: #22282C; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #C2410C; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Low-emphasis inline link, e.g. 'Learn more →' on service cards.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; background: none; border: none; color: #C2410C; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; text-decoration: none; padding: 0.75rem 0; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { text-decoration: underline; text-underline-offset: 4px; }

narrative.overview: Mirano's interface reads like an audited record, not a sales pitch. Every claim is dated, sourced, and specific: named partners, exact engagement dates, capped team sizes, a live product URL — the same discipline the company applies to the software it ships. The Hero's own copy calls its project/product lists a "ledger of engagements," and that idea sets the tone for the whole system: entries, not slogans. The system explicitly rejects the generic agency/SaaS template look — stock-photo consultancy sites, gradient-hero "AI startup" templates, bloated enterprise pages with fake testimonials and inflated team-size claims. Nothing here should read as trying to look bigger or more generic-corporate than Mirano actually is. Confidence comes from specificity, not superlatives; restraint is a feature, not a limitation.
keyCharacteristics: Warm-neutral, quiet surfaces (porcelain/limestone) that never compete with content
A single signal color (orange) used sparingly and only where it means something
Flat by default — borders and tonal layering carry structure, not shadows
One deliberate dark section per page (graphite) as the sole high-contrast beat
A recurring mono-uppercase eyebrow as the system's one precision marker

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Orange (and its gradient) is the only saturated color in the system. It appears on icons, the primary CTA, ledger status dots, and the accent line/stat numbers — never as a large background fill, never duplicated as a second brand color.

rules.name: The One Dark Section Rule
rules.body: Graphite appears at most once per page as a contrast section, plus the footer. It is not a second theme to alternate with light sections; it is a single deliberate beat.

rules.name: The PLIMA Exception
rules.body: The PLIMA feature card on /products alone carries PLIMA's own brand colors, strictly scoped to that one card, never elsewhere, and never on /references.

rules.name: The Data-Face Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for anything that reads as a data point — labels, stats, dates, meta captions. It never appears in headlines or running prose.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Cards, buttons, and sections carry no shadow at rest. Depth, where it exists at all, is a response to state (header on scroll, button hover transform), never a static decoration.

dos: Do keep Signal Orange to icons, the primary CTA, ledger status dots, accent lines, and stat numbers — never a large flat background fill.
Do use the 3px top gradient bar as the CTA card's one signature accent — top edge only, never a colored side border.
Do hold graphite to one contrast section per page plus the footer.
Do keep JetBrains Mono strictly for labels, stats, dates, and the eyebrow — never headlines or prose.
Do let structure come from borders and background tone shifts, not shadows; reserve shadow for the header's scroll state only.
Do scope PLIMA's violet/green brand colors strictly to the PLIMA card on /products.
Do support all three locales (DE/EN/HR) for any new copy or component.
donts: Don't introduce a second saturated brand color alongside Signal Orange.
Don't add drop shadows to cards or buttons at rest.
Don't use border-left/border-right accent stripes on cards or list items.
Don't reach for gradient text beyond the existing .stat-number pattern.
Don't build a generic agency/SaaS template look — stock photos, gradient-mesh AI-startup backgrounds, testimonial carousels, or unbacked growth claims.
Don't default to a cream/sand/beige body background 'for warmth' — Porcelain stays low-chroma.
Don't apply glassmorphism decoratively elsewhere — the sticky header's blur is the one purposeful instance.
